units.title: Closed-ball spherical mean value
units.reader_note: Real source specialization with an independently identified direct proof route; derivatives belong to the retained extension.
units.statement: A function with a harmonic extension near a positive closed ball equals the normalized spherical average of its boundary values at the center.
assumptions: There is an actual function \(v\), harmonic near every point of \(K=\overline B(a,R)\), with \(v=u\) on \(K\). The original \(u\) has no imposed regularity or measurability outside \(K\).

\(\sigma\) is the normalized surface law on \(S^{n-1}=\{\zeta\in\mathbb R^n:\|\zeta\|=1\}\), characterized in the source as the unique Borel probability invariant under every orthogonal transformation. Its literal Lean realization and integrability are justified internally.

notation.text: The existing polar sphere measure, its exact normalization, and the spherical average of one retained extension.

steps.title: Retain the same actual extension
steps.text: Consume the existing zero-flux theorem once. Its returned extension is fixed before all subradii; retain its neighborhood harmonicity and equality with u on the entire parent ball. This returned witness, rather than a radius-dependent choice, defines M.
steps.lean: The public proof obtains v,hv,hvu,hflux from harmonic_closedBall_zero_flux before defining M.

steps.title: Identify the actual normalized source law
steps.text: Use the identical canonical Haar-column/surface identity and Haar left invariance. The mapped normalized sphere measure is an actual Haar column probability; a fixed orthogonal transformation corresponds to left multiplication. Transfer the resulting invariance back through the measurable sphere inclusion. Thus the exact literal mu is a Borel probability invariant under all source orthogonal transformations, so the source uniqueness characterization identifies it with sigma. The canonical finite nonzero polar law is used; equality of masses alone is not the argument.
steps.lean: sphereRotation is the actual norm-preserving matrix action. normalized_sphere_law calls column_map_eq_normalized_surface and orthogonalHaar_map_mul_left, derives probability through the measurable inclusion, and proves the exact sphere map identity by map_injective. No new law is defined by invariance.

steps.title: Keep every observation inside the compact parent ball
steps.text: For t in the closed radius interval and unit zeta, a+t zeta lies in K. Actual local C2 of v gives continuity of v and its Frechet derivative there. Compactness bounds the derivative operator norm internally. The sphere sections are continuous and genuinely integrable for the finite normalized law.
steps.lean: affine_sphere_mem proves membership. sphere_section_continuous uses actual local C2. spherical_mean_hasDerivAt obtains C from isCompact_closedBall.exists_bound_of_continuousOn applied to the actual fderiv.

steps.title: Retain continuity at both endpoint radii
steps.text: The selected extension composed with the affine sphere map is jointly continuous on the closed parameter interval times the compact sphere. The actual compact-parametric-integral theorem derives a common integrable value bound and continuity of M, including t=0 and t=R. No endpoint derivative is assumed.
steps.lean: spherical_mean_continuous restricts the parameter type to Icc0R, proves joint continuity, and invokes continuous_parametric_integral_of_continuous with the compact sphere. Its actual domination proof supplies the value-integral semantics.

steps.title: Differentiate the actual integral in the interior
steps.text: On the open interval (0,R), the radial chain rule gives derivative Dv(a+t zeta)[zeta]. The compact parent-ball operator bound and unit norm give a constant L1 derivative dominator on a common parameter neighborhood. Section measurability, value L1 and derivative measurability are established before differentiating under the integral. The Riesz identity identifies the derivative with the gradient pairing.
steps.lean: spherical_mean_hasDerivAt derives hdc,hC,hFc,hmeas,hint,hbound,hdiff and calls hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le on Ioo0R. That open interval is an actual common neighborhood at each interior point; the theorem derives its smaller ball. No bound is a public hypothesis.

steps.title: Use zero flux and the real mean value theorem
steps.text: Scale the same extension zero-flux integral from tau to the exact mu. This makes the actual derivative of M zero at every interior radius. Closed-interval continuity and interior differentiability meet the real mean value theorem hypotheses, yielding equality between the outer and center averages. Both source dimensions n=2 and n>2 are covered by this direct route; the unused author power/log proofs remain separately represented.
steps.lean: The public hd uses integral_smul_measure and hflux. exists_hasDerivAt_eq_slope supplies the endpoint slope; positivity of R cancels its denominator. There is no derivative requirement at either endpoint.

steps.title: Evaluate the center and transfer only values
steps.text: Actual probability gives M(0)=v(a). At the center and every outer-sphere observation, EqOn identifies v with u. Derive the original sampled-u L1 from the continuous v section and this equality, then transfer its actual integral. No derivative or ambient regularity is transferred to u.
steps.lean: hcenter uses the probability instance. hsample, hvint and huint prove value equality and actual restricted integrability; integral_congr_ae transfers the boundary integral, and mem_closedBall_self supplies the center value.

units.lean_statement: The exact pre-proof V2 statement: original total u with one existential matching harmonic-neighborhood extension and no off-ball constraint.
